children: Government engineering solutions provider Amentum Holdings
will be announcing earnings results this Monday afternoon. Here’s what you need to know.

Amentum missed analysts’ revenue expectations last quarter, reporting revenues of $3.49 billion, down 2% year on year. It was an underwhelming quarter for the company, with a significant miss of analysts’ EPS estimates.
Is Amentum a buy or sell going into earnings?

params.linkText: Read our full analysis here, it’s free for active Edge members

children: This quarter, the market is expecting Amentum’s revenue to decline 5.9% year on year, a reversal from the 10.1% increase it recorded in the same quarter last year.

Analysts covering the company have generally reconfirmed their estimates over the last 30 days, suggesting they anticipate the business will stay the course heading into earnings. Amentum has missed Wall Street’s revenue estimates multiple times over the last two years.

Looking at Amentum’s peers in the government & technical consulting segment, some have already reported their Q3 results, giving us a hint as to what we can expect. Booz Allen Hamilton’s revenues decreased 3.9% year on year, missing analysts’ expectations by 1.1%, and Maximus reported a revenue decline of 1.3%, in line with consensus estimates. Booz Allen Hamilton traded up 6.1% following the results while Maximus was down 3.8%.

Over the last year or so, investors' attention has moved from one major market theme to the next, spanning AI disruption and surging infrastructure investment to geopolitical tensions, interest rates, and the health of the broader economy. While some of the government & technical consulting stocks have shown solid performance in this choppy environment, the group has generally underperformed, with share prices down 9.5% on average over the last month. Amentum is down 6.4% during the same time and is heading into earnings with an average analyst price target of $29.25 (compared to the current share price of $20.38).
